title: Duplicated Invariants Across Multiple Initializers
pattern: Multiple constructor/initializer functions in a struct separately validating invariants and assigning duplicate fields.
why_bad: If a new validation rule or a new field is introduced, a developer must remember to update every constructor function. Forgetting one results in uninitialized fields or broken invariants.
detection: Multiple `impl` constructors containing textually identical guard assertions, validation checks, or duplicate struct instantiation blocks.
counterexample: Builders that accumulate transient state before passing validation inside a single unified `.build()` consumer.
